UCB1 policy

Source: R/policies-etc-ucb-thompson.R
policy_ucb1.Rd

The upper confidence bound policy of Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer (2002). After one initial pull of each arm, it selects the arm maximising $$\hat{\mu}_a + \sqrt{2 \log t / n_a},$$ where \(\hat{\mu}_a\) is the sample-average reward of arm \(a\), \(n_a\) its pull count and \(t\) the current step. Ties are broken uniformly at random.

Usage

policy_ucb1()

Value

A bandit_policy object.

Details

The classical regret analysis assumes rewards bounded in [0, 1] and a stationary environment; the implementation accepts any numeric rewards but the theoretical guarantee does not transfer automatically.

References

Auer, P., Cesa-Bianchi, N., Fischer, P. (2002). Finite-time analysis of the multiarmed bandit problem. Machine Learning 47(2-3), 235-256. doi:10.1023/A:1013689704352

See also

policy_thompson(), policy_epsilon_greedy()

Examples

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(a = 0.2, b = 0.5))
run_experiment(env, policy_ucb1(), horizon = 500, seed = 1)
#> <bandit_result> 1 policy x 1 replicate x horizon 500 (seed 1)
#> environment: bernoulli_environment (2 arms)
#> stored: summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   policy      replications mean_regret median_regret regret_q025 regret_q975
#> * <chr>              <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 ucb1_policy            1        17.4          17.4        17.4        17.4
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_reward <dbl>, mean_optimal_share <dbl>
